title: South Sudanese community demands answers after police-involved shooting
article: Winnipeg's South Sudanese community is demanding answers after one of their own was fatally shot after a confrontation with Winnipeg Police on Saturday morning at his suite in an apartment building on Colony Street just north of Broadway.
Community officials identified the deceased man as 43-year-old Machuar Mawien Madut, a father of three who had immigrated to Winnipeg as a refugee from South Sudan in 2003.

"This community has been heart-broken and they are being torn, not just by this incident but by many incidents," said Martino Laku, President of Council of South Sudanese Community of Manitoba (COSSCOM) at a press conference at the COSSCOM community centre on Monday. "They have families back home and every day and every week they receive sad news of loved ones who lost their life. This incident here actually broke their hearts. It made them really angry because this guy fled his home to be here safe with his family but eventually his life ended this way."
Members of the local community gathered for the press conference to express their anger and sadness over Madut's death.
"We're really sad as a community for him to have to leave this way," said community member Sandy Deng.
After arriving in Winnipeg, Madut moved to Brooks, Alta., to work at a meat processing plant for two years before returning here in 2012.

Community members said that Madut had been having mental health issues recently due to the breakup of his marriage. Last week, community members were coordinating efforts with health experts to get him the help he needed.
But they wondered why more wasn't done by police to deescalate the situation.

"We know that he had a rough time with the police but we believe that this could have had a different outcome, a positive outcome," said Laku. "The police are trained and they are aware of mental illness and they could deescalate the situation and they could talk him out of it and saved his life. But this went into a negative way, in a way that we don't understand."

"I don't really trust the police because we assume that they have all the resources to help people with mental issues, deal with people with different backgrounds," said Ayei Madut, who trying to get friend help from the Winnipeg Regional Health Authority Crisis Response Centre on Bannatyne on the day that he was shot.

"Because in this situation, I can do better than whatever they did. It's simple. You don't have to be a doctor to diagnose the situation. We know it's physical, you know how to be tough but you have to think."
Winnipeg Police Service were referring all inquiries to the Independent Investigation Unit (IIU) of Manitoba on Monday.

According to a press release from the IIU on Monday, police notified them on Saturday that at around 9:43 a.m., their officers responded to a report of a male armed with a hammer and a potential break-in at a suite on Colony Street. Police said a confrontation with the male took place and resulted in an officer or officers discharging their firearms. He was taken to Health Sciences Centre where he was later pronounced dead.
A team of IIU investigators was immediately deployed to the scene. Since this matter involves a fatality, a request for a civilian monitor will be made to the Manitoba Police Commission.
Deng disputes the police's contention that he was trying to break into his own apartment.

"This is a typical stereotype," said Deng."For a lot of people who come from marginalized communities, there is always a justification for a shooting. I was hoping that the police would give us a better picture of what really happened. But he was a human being, he was supposed to be supported. He was one day away from going to see a mental health specialist."

Community members believe he may have been attempting to repair a broken door with the hammer although they concede that he may have been in an agitated state and was throwing household items into the back lane of the apartment building. A smashed stove and refrigerator were visible at the scene.
Witnesses or other individuals who have information or video footage that may assist this investigation are asked to contact the IIU toll free at 1-844-667-6060.
A rally is planned for Friday at a time and place to be determined.
